name: Isotretinoin

lead: Isotretinoin (13-cis retinoic acid, formerly sold as Accutane) is an oral retinoid reserved for severe, scarring or treatment-resistant acne. It is the only acne therapy capable of producing long-lasting remission in many patients and is also used off-label for severe rosacea and some other conditions.
In looksmaxxing circles it is discussed as a decisive treatment for severe acne, although its side-effect burden and regulatory controls make it a medically supervised, not casual, option.

paras: Isotretinoin dramatically shrinks sebaceous glands and lowers sebum output, normalizes follicular keratinization, reduces growth of acne-associated bacteria indirectly by changing the follicular environment, and has anti-inflammatory effects. It likely acts partly through induction of cell death in sebocytes and changes in retinoid-responsive gene expression.

It is a potent teratogen and is distributed under strict risk-management programs (such as iPLEDGE in the US) requiring pregnancy prevention. Common effects include dry lips, skin and eyes; laboratory monitoring is needed for lipids and liver enzymes. Reports of mood changes have been studied extensively, and a recent meta-analysis found no clear increase in suicide risk, though monitoring remains standard. It is prescription-only.
